doc.title: Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Oneonta, New York, December 28, 2005

title: Joining Paul Whiteman: hotels, Woodbury radio show and the sax section
summary: Joining Whiteman in spring 1936, Billy Rose's Jumbo, Adolph Deutsch, and the five-man sax section.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel

blocks.x: Oh well with the Whiteman band hotel rooms were so reasonable. We used to get a rate. $2.50 single. Not the Waldorf, but good hotels. No flea bags. Like Goldie used to say, no flea bags you know. And it was great traveling with the band, the Whiteman band. And I’ll never forget. See I joined spring of ’36. But I was doing the radio show. Woodbury Hollow Soap Hour. And I just did that. The rest of the band, they were doing Jumbo. Billy Rose’s Jumbo at the Hippodrome Theater, it was on Sixth Avenue just north of 42nd Street. The old Hippodrome. And they were doing that show. And every week I just did the broadcast. Adolph Deutsch was his main arranger. He finally went to Hollywood and made it big there. Ramona was in the band. I can tell you every musician that was in the band. Five saxes. Jack Cordero tenor; George Bandford from Boston, flute and tenor; Charlie Strickfaden oboe and baritone; Frankie Trumbauer and I sat next, together, and that was it, he was a wonderful guy and a wonderful player.
